'''Zu Geng''' or '''Zu Gengzhi''' ({{zh|c=祖暅之|w=Tsu Keng-chih}}; ca. 480 – ca. 525) was a Chinese mathematician, politician, and writer. His [[courtesy name]] was '''Jingshuo''' ({{zh|t=景爍|labels=no}}). He was the son of the famous mathematician [[Zu Chongzhi]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=http://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/1073908/Zu-Gengzhi| title=Zu Gengzhi |encyclopedia=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |access-date=2014-09-22}}</ref> He is known principally for deriving and proving the formula for the volume of a sphere. He additionally measured the angular distance between [[Polaris]] and the [[Celestial pole|celestial north pole]], which was greater 1600 years ago than it is today.
